questions.question: Why is 'offline-first' a more central concern for mobile apps than for most web apps?
options: Mobile devices cannot connect to WiFi
Mobile usage routinely involves real connectivity loss (subways, flights, dead zones), so offline is a normal state to design for, not an edge case
AsyncStorage doesn't work without an internet connection
App stores require offline support for approval
questions.explanation: Mobile users regularly experience genuine connectivity loss as part of normal use, which is why offline-first treats local data as the primary source of truth rather than an afterthought.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of AsyncStorage compared to an embedded database like SQLite?
options: AsyncStorage has no querying capability beyond exact key lookups, making filtering or relational data awkward at scale
AsyncStorage data is lost when the app closes
questions.explanation: AsyncStorage is a flat key-value store; anything resembling a query (filter, join, relationship) has to be done manually in JS after loading everything, which doesn't scale well.

questions.question: In the optimistic local-write pattern shown, why does the UI render the new note before the API call to the server resolves?
options: It's a bug that should be fixed
The local database is treated as the source of truth, so the UI reflects the user's action immediately rather than waiting on a network round-trip
The API call is not actually necessary
React Native requires all UI updates to happen before any async call
questions.explanation: Offline-first design makes the local write authoritative for the UI; the network sync happens in the background and updates a sync status flag rather than blocking the user-visible update.

questions.question: What does a layer like WatermelonDB add on top of raw SQLite?
options: Nothing — it's just a renamed version of SQLite
An observable, React-friendly query layer plus built-in sync primitives, so components can subscribe to a query and re-render automatically as local data changes
It replaces SQL queries with AsyncStorage key-value lookups
It removes the need for any local database at all
questions.explanation: WatermelonDB builds on SQLite's storage but adds reactive, observable queries and sync-aware primitives, so UI components update automatically as the underlying data changes, whether from the user or a background sync.
